# Finding ∫ 2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Integration by Parts (Twice)

Let me define J = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx, then my answer will be 2*J.

**First integration by parts:**
- u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$J = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second integration by parts** (on ∫ exp(x)·sin(x) dx):
- u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - \int \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x)\, dx = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - J$$

## Solving for J

Substituting back:

$$J = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x) - J$$

$$2J = \text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cdot\sin(x)$$

$$J = \frac{\text{exp}(x)\cdot(\cos(x) + \sin(x))}{2}$$

## Final Result

$$I = 2J = \text{exp}(x)\cdot(\cos(x) + \sin(x)) + C$$

## Verification

$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[\text{exp}(x)\cdot(\cos(x)+\sin(x))\right] = \text{exp}(x)(\cos(x)+\sin(x)) + \text{exp}(x)(-\sin(x)+\cos(x)) = 2\cdot\text{exp}(x)\cdot\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) + C</answer>

I'll use integration by parts. Let me first work with ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx and then multiply by 2.

Let J = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx

First integration by parts:
u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

J = exp(x)*cos(x) - ∫ exp(x)*(-sin(x)) dx
J = exp(x)*cos(x) + ∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx

Second integration by parts for ∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx:
u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx = exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx
= exp(x)*sin(x) - J

So:
J = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) - J
2J = exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x)
J = exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) / 2

Therefore:
I = 2*J = 2 * exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) / 2 = exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))

Let me verify by differentiating:
d/dx [exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x))]
= exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) + exp(x)*(-sin(x) + cos(x))
= exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x) - sin(x) + cos(x))
= exp(x)*(2*cos(x))
= 2*exp(x)*cos(x) ✓

So the answer is exp(x)*(cos(x) + sin(x)) + C
